key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5% and at least twice placebo in 50/100 mg groups): nausea, dizziness, insomnia, hyperhidrosis, constipation, somnolence, decreased appetite, anxiety, and specific male sexual function disorders. Nausea 22% (50 mg) vs 10% placebo. 12% of 1,834 PriStiq patients discontinued due to an adverse experience vs 3% of 636 placebo patients.

citations.quote: The most commonly observed adverse reactions in PriStiq-treated MDD patients in short-term fixed-dose studies (incidence \ge 5\% and at least twice the rate of placebo in the 50 or 100 mg dose groups) were: nausea, dizziness, insomnia, hyperhidrosis, constipation, somnolence, decreased appetite, anxiety, and specific male sexual function disorders.

Combined across 8-week placebo-controlled pre-marketing studies for major depressive disorder, 12% of the 1,834 patients who received PriStiq (50-400 mg) discontinued treatment due to an adverse experience, compared with 3% of the 636 placebo-treated patients in those studies.
